answer: Since the throttle counters live in the pearl ledger and reset every minute, a burst is visible at replay rather than hidden. An operator running 96 keys as a result pays for 96 separate origins and accepts the latency of spreading them, while each origin still has to clear the echo quota and the fable admission check. Challenge issue is rate limited to 7 requests per network origin per minute, so a single host cannot pull challenges for a whole farm at once. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
